decision_note: This is a commercial test portfolio, not a guarantee of future sales. TEST_NOW means the offer has enough evidence to justify a lean paid-market test. Only paid validation may promote it to SELL_NOW.

control_room_subscription.reason: Current GC commercial-integrity policy says no public recurring subscription until a complete paid matter is field-verified.

test_now.buyer: SME contractor, supplier or service business with an invoice or payment milestone at risk
test_now.urgent_problem: Payment is delayed, challenged or likely to be challenged while proof is scattered.

strengths: Output is concrete and easy to demo
Existing GC delivery is already scoped around evidence maps, proof gaps and an invoice defence file
weaknesses: May need professional review when legal conclusions are requested
Value is weaker when the client has no underlying proof
opportunities: 2026 construction-market evidence shows delayed payments remain a material operational problem
Can lead naturally into claim readiness without inventing a new product
threats: Traditional lawyers, claims consultants and internal commercial teams compete for the same budget
Poor source records can make the result less useful
Overclaiming legal effect would breach GC's professional boundary

demand_evidence.source: Industry Insight Preferred Supplier Survey, 4 Aug 2026
demand_evidence.signal: Contractors on 38 active projects worth about R11bn reported payment delays among the pressures affecting project delivery.

demand_evidence.source: MDA Attorneys analysis reported by Polity, 19 May 2026
demand_evidence.signal: Payment failures were the largest category in the firm's construction adjudication caseload.

test_now.buyer: Contractor, subcontractor, supplier or SME facing a live payment, delay or scope dispute
test_now.urgent_problem: A dispute is forming and the business needs chronology, notices and evidence organised before leverage is lost.

strengths: Urgent use case with a clear deadline
Uses existing GC chronology, notice and evidence capabilities
weaknesses: Buyer may already be in lawyer-led dispute mode
Document volume can increase delivery cost
Professional review may be required for legal conclusions
opportunities: Payment and delay disputes create a natural trigger for purchase
Can reduce time spent preparing a matter for external counsel
threats: Outside counsel may bundle this work into legal fees
Late-stage disputes can contain missing facts that cannot be recreated
A generic pack would fail if contract form and edition are not respected

demand_evidence.source: MDA Attorneys analysis reported by Polity, 19 May 2026
demand_evidence.signal: Payment failures were the dominant dispute category in the reported adjudication caseload, with extension-of-time issues also material.

demand_evidence.source: Industry Insight Preferred Supplier Survey, 4 Aug 2026
demand_evidence.signal: Delayed payments and administrative bottlenecks were reported across active South African construction projects.

test_now.buyer: Construction contractor or subcontractor working under a notice-driven contract
test_now.urgent_problem: A live event has triggered contractual notice clocks and the team risks missing them.

strengths: Easy before-and-after demo: event to trigger to notice calendar
weaknesses: Narrower buyer segment than general contract review
Accuracy depends on exact contract form, edition and amendments
opportunities: Can be a wedge into broader obligation and claim-readiness work
Construction procurement and delivery remain procedurally complex
threats: Calendar/reminder tools are cheaper substitutes when the contract logic is simple
A missed or wrongly mapped trigger can create material risk
Professional responsibility boundaries must stay explicit

demand_evidence.source: cidb procurement prescripts and Draft SFU 2026
demand_evidence.signal: South African construction procurement operates under detailed public-sector prescripts and updated procedural requirements.

demand_evidence.source: Industry Insight Preferred Supplier Survey, 4 Aug 2026
demand_evidence.signal: Administrative bottlenecks and delivery delays remain active project problems, increasing the value of disciplined notice control.

parked.buyer: Founder-led SME or commercial team about to sign a material customer, supplier or project deal
parked.urgent_problem: The business needs a fast view of money, authority, dates, notices and proof before signature.

strengths: Pre-signing trigger is easy to understand
Existing output is concrete and bounded
weaknesses: Buyer may not perceive risk until a problem occurs
opportunities: Can become the front door for GC without a subscription commitment
Can expose downstream needs such as obligation control or payment proof
threats: Free AI contract summaries can anchor buyer expectations at zero
Legal-advice boundaries may confuse buyers if messaging is not precise
Long bespoke contracts can erode fixed-fee margin

demand_evidence.source: SpotDraft State of Legal Ops summary, Sep 2026
demand_evidence.signal: Contract turnaround and budget constraints remain major legal-operations concerns for lean teams.
The product is already implemented as a fixed-scope 2–4 business-day offer rather than a new concept.

parked.park_reason: Broad pre-signing need is less urgent than cash/payment/claims and current independent demand evidence is not strong enough for a fast-sell test.

mn.commercial_rule: Do not create a new exam-season SKU. Test the existing MN+ 30-day pass and use Matric exam rescue only as a campaign/use-case angle. Grade 12 core learning and the existing free Matric paper hub remain free.

test_now.blocker: Live Yoco credentials, registered webhook and controlled live payment proof are not yet verified.
test_now.buyer: South African parent or caregiver wanting a low-cost month of premium learning support
test_now.urgent_problem: A learner needs focused repair and exam support without the hourly cost of private tutoring.
test_now.campaign_angle: Matric exam rescue may be used as a time-sensitive acquisition angle, but it is not a separate paid SKU and may not paywall the free Grade 12 core.

strengths: Very low price relative to private tutoring
Existing 30-day product and entitlement code already exist
MN already has free original Matric Maths mock sets and Physical Sciences mocks plus a paper-to-repair workflow
weaknesses: Live payment release is not yet proven
Grade 12 broader product remains beta and cannot be marketed as a turnkey Matric school
Free Grade 12 core reduces the amount of content that can legitimately sit behind the paywall
opportunities: 2026 NSC exams begin in October, creating a real time-sensitive preparation window
Private tutoring prices create a strong affordability contrast for families seeking supplemental help
threats: A current local competitor markets AI Matric preparation at R149 per month
Parents may default to free past papers or general AI tools
Any claim that implies guaranteed marks or complete CAPS coverage would be misleading

demand_evidence.source: Department of Basic Education 2026 NSC timetable
demand_evidence.signal: The October/November 2026 NSC examination cycle begins in mid-October, creating an immediate exam-preparation window.
Private Grade 12 tutoring averaged hundreds of rand per hour, with Matric Mathematics materially higher, supporting an affordability pain point.
A South African AI Matric-prep competitor publicly charges R149 per month, showing a live paid category.

product_truth: MN+ 30-day pass is coded at R99 and non-recurring.
Free Grade 12 core learning remains R0.
MN has original Maths mock sets 001–005, Physical Sciences mock 001 and a paper-to-repair workflow.
Grade 12 remains beta and requires further field testing and subject materialisation before any turnkey-school claim.
